At Warner Records, he’ll take on the role of vice chairman, reporting to chairman/CEO Aaron Bay-Schuck . A nearly 30-year veteran of Universal Music Group (UMG), the parent company of Republic Records, Roppo has held roles in sales, marketing and commerce at Island Def Jam Music Group (IDJ) and Republic before being promoted to the Republic executive team. summary: Amazon's new Kindle Page-Turn Cover promises extra convenience, but our readers have strong opinions about the price tag.
body: Credit: Amazon Physical page-turn buttons might seem like a pretty basic feature for an e-reader , but Amazon has spent years leaving them off its Kindle lineup. The company has given bookworms a way to bring them back with its latest devices, although it’s charging a hefty premium for the privilege. We recently asked readers whether they’d be willing to pay $80 for this convenience, and the results suggest Amazon might have misread the room. As my colleague Dhruv Bhutani explained in his recent look at the 2026 Kindle refresh , Amazon’s new Page-Turn Cover adds physical buttons to the e-reader through a magnetic connection. The catch is that it costs $80 and it only works with the Signature Editions of the Kindle Paperwhite and Colorsoft, which already cost $250 and $320, respectively. We wanted to know whether you thought this was fair enough, or if perhaps Amazon should have just included this functionality as part of the deal.

title: Google will pay you up to $20,000 for Chrome security bugs
summary: It's also adding new categories to the reward program.
body: TL;DR Google is quadrupling the base reward amount for reporting critical Chrome vulnerabilities. It is also introducing rewards of up to $20,000 for high-impact bugs. End-of-year awards will celebrate submissions from the community. Google has relied on vulnerability reports from security researchers alongside its own internal security teams to keep apps like Chrome secure against exploits. The company has made several changes to its Vulnerability Rewards Program (VRP) over the last few months, including reducing Chrome reward payouts in May and using AI to improve Chrome security in July. Now, the company is making further adjustments to the Chrome VRP. In a blog post, the company announces new reward amounts and categories. Google has quadrupled the base reward amount for memory corruption vulnerabilities to $2,000. Furthermore, reports for controlled reads and crashes in the browser, GPU, and network processes will now earn rewards of $4,000. Payouts for controlled writes, on the other hand, can go up to $20,000.

Android foldables have used graphite sheets as part of the display stack or on the chassis on either side of the spine, but have not typically used the spine itself for cooling. Foldables have spent years balancing thinner profiles with flagship-grade SoCs and the resulting thermal dilemma. When unfolded, you have a large surface area that is great for thermal dissipation, but when folded, you create a thermal sandwich that suddenly has to work with only half the surface area.
